answer.heading: My research conclusion
answer.text: VTI's available history is too short to simulate your 7-year horizon, so evidence cannot establish typical or worst-case outcomes for that period. Over the observed 2021–2026 window, VTI rose 87.43% in CAD and recovered from a 23.59% drawdown in 608 days, but without a full 84-month rolling window no historical path tests your actual timeline or shows whether a 7-year hold would have met a home-purchase target.

answer.heading: What supports this view
answer.text: The historical_market tool confirms annualized volatility of 17.13%, worst 12-month return of -15.57%, and worst 36-month return of +28.04%, showing VTI can swing sharply but recovered positively over three years. Between 2021-11-30 and 2026-09-29, nominal CAD return was +91.12% and inflation-adjusted return was +62.11% after Canadian CPI rose 17.89%, preserving real purchasing power in that retrospective period.

answer.heading: What argues against it
answer.text: The 2022 decline produced a -14.03% return and 22.98% drawdown, and early 2025 saw -16.73% return with 20.04% drawdown. Because you have not decided how much loss you could absorb, these historical drops may exceed your undetermined capacity, risking forced sale or shortfall at the home-purchase date if a similar decline occurs near year seven.

answer.heading: Important gaps and next step
answer.text: History cannot establish a future loss limit or confirm VTI will meet a long-term goal. The missing 7-year rolling-window data means no evidence shows best, worst, or median outcomes for your timeline. Decide your maximum acceptable dollar loss and whether you have reserve funds outside the 5,700 CAD; that will clarify whether VTI's observed drawdowns fit your capacity and whether a shorter-duration or less-volatile alternative better matches your fixed home-purchase deadline.

VTI.budget.title: What your amount represents in VTI
VTI.budget.text: Used entirely for this one asset, CAD 5,700.00 corresponds to approximately 10 whole shares at the observed price, leaving CAD 409.08 before fees and currency spreads. This is an indicative sizing calculation, not an order or a forecast. This current-price whole-share estimate is separate from the historical replay, which invests the full stated amount in fractional units at its starting date. It uses the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate dated 2026-11-13; the FX and equity observations are not simultaneous.
